# DevSecOps Challenge 1 — DevSecOps with Coding Agents at Papaya

## Note

- You are required to use a coding agent (e.g. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) to complete this challenge.
- If you have any issues or questions, don't hesitate to contact us.

## Context

Papaya builds a GenAI-powered enterprise platform for the insurance industry — Claim, Underwriting, Policy Servicing, and FWA (Fraud/Waste/Abuse) — serving insurer partners across SEA and Asia. Our platform processes sensitive data every day: medical documents, diagnoses, claim histories, national IDs, and bank accounts of insured members.

Every engineer at Papaya works agent-first: Claude Code (Team Premium) is the primary tool for writing code, running git, opening PRs, and increasingly for infrastructure work.

This is where we are today (see [Appendix A](#appendix-a--papaya-platform-context) for the full picture):

- Engineers run Claude Code on their laptops, signed in to AWS through their SSO profiles. Most engineers' profiles can reach production.
- Some engineers run Claude Code with permission prompts turned off because "it is faster".
- Engineers install MCP servers and plugins they find useful; there is no review process.
- CI/CD runs on GitHub Actions. Some workflows use a long-lived GitHub token and AWS access keys stored as repository secrets.
- Monitoring and alerting exist but are fragmented across CloudWatch, GCP, and Slack channels. On-call is informal.
- We are working towards ISO 27001 and must satisfy HIPAA and regional data-protection regulations for our partners.

We've heard two strong opinions from inside the company:

> **Engineering:** "Let Claude Code talk to AWS directly. I want to debug and ship my own infra changes without waiting for someone else."
>
> **Compliance:** "Nothing changes in production — by a human or an agent — without a named person who reviewed and approved it."

## Problem

You are joining as our DevSecOps Engineer. Your first mission: **design the framework and workflow for how Papaya uses coding agents for DevSecOps.**

You don't have access to our systems or code, and we don't expect you to.

## Requirements

- The format of the deliverable is up to you.

## Submission

Submit everything in **one GitHub repository** and send us the link. Other channels (cloud storage, email attachments) are not accepted.

The repository must contain:

- Your deliverable(s).
- The **complete, raw, unedited conversation(s)** with your coding agent — every session you used for this challenge. Native session files are preferred (e.g. Claude Code: `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl`; Codex CLI: `~/.codex/sessions/`); for chat apps, commit an export of the conversation.

**Submissions without the agent conversation will be automatically marked as failed.**

---

## Appendix A — Papaya Platform Context

### Cloud

- **AWS (primary):** Lambda (Serverless Framework), ECS, EC2, Aurora PostgreSQL, SNS, SQS, Step Functions, S3 (claim documents), CloudWatch.
- **GCP:** Vertex AI and Gemini API workloads for document AI and ML models.
- **Kubernetes ([k0s](https://k0sproject.io/)):** workloads for AI agents and internal services.
- **Hosting:** Firebase Hosting for web frontends.

### Application

- **Backend:** Node.js, TypeScript, GraphQL (Apollo Server, Hasura), PostgreSQL.
- **Frontend / Mobile:** Next.js, React, React Native (Expo).
- **AI/ML:** Python, PyTorch, OpenAI, Vertex AI, Gemini, Claude.
- **AI agents in production:** claim assessment, document extraction and classification, FWA detection — they read documents uploaded by partners and members.

### Engineering

- **Source control & CI/CD:** a single monorepo on GitHub for the whole system — apps, web, backend, mobile, AI/ML, and Infrastructure as Code ([Pulumi](https://www.pulumi.com/), plus [Serverless Framework](https://www.serverless.com/) for Lambda functions); GitHub Actions for CI/CD.
- **Coding agent:** Claude Code (Team Premium) for every engineer; internal Claude Code plugins are distributed via a plugin marketplace.
- **Work tracking & communication:** Linear, Slack.
- **Tenancy:** multiple insurer partners across countries (e.g. Vietnam, Thailand, Hong Kong), each with their own data and contractual requirements.

### Compliance

- ISO 27001 (in progress), HIPAA, and regional data-protection regulations in the countries we operate in.

# Architecture decision records

Each record states one major decision behind [`../framework.md`](../framework.md), the options weighed
and what it costs. Details and the full evidence live in the framework; an ADR only records the
choice. Markers follow the framework legend: 📖 R*x.y* = documented research row in
`work/02-research.md`, ⚠️ = inference or unverified, [design] = proposal of this submission. OD*n* = owner
decisions in the framework's last table; D1–D3 = owner decisions in research 6.6. Other codes (GĐ-n
assumptions, S-n success criteria, P-n problems, G-n gaps, Options §n, framing §n) are explained in the
framework's "How to read this" section.

| ADR | Decision | Framework layer |
|---|---|---|
| [0001](0001-prod-changes-only-through-ci.md) | Every production change goes through a reviewed PR applied by CI ("IaC first") | 3, 5 |
| [0002](0002-no-standing-prod-write-read-only-agent-identity.md) | Nobody holds standing prod write; in prod the only standing role (the engineer's, so the agent's) reads metadata | 1, 2 |
| [0003](0003-merge-to-main-is-the-approval-gate.md) | The merge to `main` is the approval gate: two people, code owners, on-call co-ownership | 3 |
| [0004](0004-risk-stop-on-risky-prod-diffs.md) | Risky prod diffs stop the deploy until a stack owner approves the prod preview | 3 |
| [0005](0005-break-glass-is-time-limited-jit.md) | Break-glass is a time-limited, approved JIT grant, for incidents only | 7 |
| [0006](0006-mcp-and-plugins-only-from-allowlist.md) | MCP servers and plugins are allowed only from a reviewed, pinned catalogue | 4 |
| [0007](0007-agent-settings-are-hygiene-not-the-boundary.md) | Claude Code managed settings are hygiene, not the security boundary | 2 |
| [0008](0008-oidc-no-long-lived-ci-keys.md) | CI uses OIDC; no long-lived CI keys, with one time-boxed exception | 1, 5 |
| [0009](0009-agent-stays-outside-phi.md) | The coding agent stays outside PHI; real-data reads are approved per tenant | 1, 6 |
| [0010](0010-risk-level-decides-who-approves.md) | Risk level decides who approves, not how many; non-prod needs no approval | 3 |

Not recorded as ADRs, because they follow from the decisions above: the audit chain (change records,
monthly reconciliation, drift detection; framework layer 7) the rollout plan (layer 8) and the CI-agent setup
(layer 5; covered in parts by ADR-0006 and ADR-0007).

Rule: an accepted ADR is not edited. A changed decision gets a new ADR that supersedes the old one.

### Vòng 1

Người dùng trả lời trong chat, session 2 (2026-11-08).

## Review of work/05-deliverable-plan.md

**Checked and correct:** These claims in the plan hold up:
- §0 numbers (`wc -w`):
  - framework 11,026 words and 779 lines
  - threat model 3,039 words with 20 T-rows
  - problem-control map 3,194 words with 40 P/A rows
  - ADRs 453–594 words each
- Review-round counts and the owner approvals of items 1–3 match `work/session-log.md`.
- The research rows say what the plan cites them for: R3.1.2, R3.2.2, R3.2.3, R3.2.5, R3.2.7, R2.1.4, R4.2.1 and R4.4.2.
- GĐ-5 (GitHub Team) is owner-confirmed.
- `claude plugin validate <path>` exists in Claude Code 2.1.319.
- I confirmed the E8 schema claim: the schemastore schema lacks `allowedProviders` and `managedSourcesBehavior`.
- `mmdc` 11.12.0 renders a test diagram to SVG (I ran it in the scratchpad).

### HIGH

**H1. §3.1 E4: the OIDC `sub` uses the old format, which contradicts the framework and owner assumption A2.**
- Problem: E4 trusts `repo:<org>/<repo>:environment:production`. The framework assumes the immutable format, which includes the owner ID and repository ID.
- Evidence:
  - `docs/framework.md:157-159`: "in its `sub` format (📖 R3.4.3, R3.4.4; immutable format assumed, ⚠️ R3.7 A2)".
  - `work/02-research.md:725` (R3.4.4): "Trust policies must match the format in use". Example: `repo:octo-org@123456/octo-repo@456789:…`.
  - `work/02-research.md` §3.7, A2: the owner assumes the new format.
- Fix:
  - Use `repo:<org>@<ORG_ID>/<repo>@<REPO_ID>:environment:production`.
  - Add a comment that older repos use the format without IDs.
  - Optionally add `job_workflow_ref`, marked ⚠️ G10.
  - The test should assert the immutable shape.

### MEDIUM

**M1. §1 #2 and §5 Q1: you cannot reach ~8k words only by moving text.**
- Problem 1, the arithmetic: moving rollout, the evidence paragraphs and the standards table removes only about 1,270 words, which leaves about 9,750, not 8,000.
- Evidence (word counts I ran):
  - rollout table plus "Phase-1 load" (`framework.md:688-712`): about 750 words
  - all "Audit evidence" paragraphs: about 390 words
  - standards table: about 130 words
- So reaching ~8k means rewriting or cutting an approved document, which goes against "chuyển (không chép)… không thêm quyết định mới".
- Problem 2, structure: moving the evidence out breaks the framework's own structure and the ADR index.
  - `framework.md:9-10` says each layer has "Audit evidence".
  - `docs/adr/README.md:3-4` says "full evidence live in the framework".
- Fix:
  - Set the target to about 9.5–10k words, or say exactly what else gets cut and that the owner must approve it again.
  - Keep a one-line evidence summary in each layer, and put the detail in the register.

**M2. §3.1 E1: the ruleset is missing "branch up to date before merge".**
- Evidence: `framework.md`, Layer 3, "Gate = merge to `main`" bullet: "Branch up to date before merge, since there is no merge queue". This follows from the owner decision "Giữ Team và bỏ merge queue" (research §3.7).
- Fix: add strict required status checks (`strict_required_status_checks_policy`) to E1 and to its test.

**M3. §3.1 E3: the checks prove less than the plan claims, and one condition the design depends on has no artifact.**
- `actionlint` and `zizmor` lint syntax and known risky patterns. They do not check the conditions in `framework.md`, Layer 3, "Merge approval = deploy approval" bullet:
  - only the deploy workflow references `production`
  - no `workflow_dispatch` ref/SHA inputs
  - one concurrency group per stack without `cancel-in-progress`
- The environment's deployment-branch rule (`main` only) is what limits which branches can use the prod role (R3.4.3 inference, `research:724`). It lives in repo settings, not in YAML, and no example shows it.
- Fix:
  - Add a Python test that checks these conditions across all workflow files.
  - Add `examples/github/environment-production.json` (REST body: a custom branch policy for `main`, no reviewers) and test it.

**M4. §3.2 E8: passing the schema check proves little about the key names.**
- Evidence (I fetched the schema): the top-level `additionalProperties` is `True`, so a misspelled key still passes.
- The schemastore schema is maintained by the community, not by Anthropic, so it is not an official source (📖).
- The "✅ 12/14" claim does not list the 14 keys or the command used.
- Fix:
  - Add a check that every top-level key is either in the schema `properties` or on an explicit 📖 allowlist with its R-row.
  - List the keys and the command in the note.

**M5. §3.1 E7: no research row documents the JSON shape of the fixtures.**
- The plan says the fixtures follow "dạng JSON của `pulumi preview --json` trong docs". But:
  - R4.1.1 (`research:951`) only lists the `--json` flag.
  - R4.4.2 only says `--json` exists "for CI consumption".
  - Neither documents the output structure.
- Hand-written fixtures also cannot show that the preview hash stays the same between runs (⚠️ Options §8).
- Rule 1 risk: the fixture fields could be invented.
- Fix (either):
  - Research the output shapes first and add 📖 rows.
  - Or define a small normalised input format, put the Pulumi/Serverless adapters behind it, and mark both ⚠️.
- In both cases, state that the fixtures do not show hash stability.

**M6. Hooks are dropped without saying so, although owner decision framing Q14 lists them.**
- Evidence: `work/01-problem-framing.md` §6, row 14: "examples/ chạy/validate được (managed settings/hooks, GitHub Actions OIDC + environment, IAM sketch, plugin manifest)". The current `README.md` also promises "Claude Code settings and hooks".
- The plan has no hooks example, and §4 does not mention hooks.
- Fix (either):
  - Add a small managed hook marked advisory (ADR-0007; fails open per `framework.md`, Layer 2, "Hard limits" bullet).
  - Or list hooks in §4 with the reason and add an owner question in §5.

**M7. Some validation tools are not installed, and §5 Q5 does not cover them.**
- Evidence: `python3 -c "import pytest"` gives `ModuleNotFoundError`.
- E10 also needs `npm ci`, which downloads `@pulumi/policy` and `@pulumi/aws`.
- Fix (either):
  - Add pytest and the npm download to Q5.
  - Or use stdlib `unittest` for the Python tests.

**M8. §2 writing order: the claim that the core does not depend on layer 5 is wrong.**
- E2 (CODEOWNERS) needs the canonical L3 path list, which is defined in layer 5 (`framework.md`, Layer 5, "CODEOWNERS" bullet).
- E3 needs the layer-5 rules on credentials, pinning and triggers.
- Yet step 3 says "lõi không phụ thuộc chúng".
- Fix:
  - Edit layer 5 together with step 1.
  - Or state that layer 5 stays frozen as input until step 3.

**M9. §3.1 E2: a naive CODEOWNERS check can pass when it should fail.**
- In CODEOWNERS, the last matching pattern wins. A later broad line, such as `/infra/** @domain @oncall` or `*`, can override process-path ownership.
- Check (b), "on-call team không xuất hiện trên path quy trình", passes on line text even when it should fail.
- Fix:
  - The test should resolve the effective owners for sample paths using last-match semantics.
  - Add a 📖 row for the precedence rule; it is not in research yet.

### LOW

- **E5, citation:** the 10,240-character limit is R2.3.4 (`research:469`), not R2.3.2. R2.3.2 is about what SCPs do not restrict.
- **E5, size test:** note that the size test is ⚠️ about whether whitespace counts; measure the minified JSON.
- **E5, Lambda actions:** `lambda:UpdateFunction*` is broader than the framework's `UpdateFunctionCode` / `UpdateFunctionConfiguration` (`framework.md:148`). Use the exact actions.
- **E5, phase and scope:** label the file phase 2, as layer 8 does. State that the outside-org write deny (`framework.md:225`, all OUs) is out of the file's scope.
- **E4, citation:** `aud = sts.amazonaws.com` comes from R3.4.1 (`research:722`), not R3.4.3/3.4.4.
- **E6, format:**
  - "không có `*`" is ambiguous: metric reads need `Resource: "*"`.
  - The test must expand wildcard actions such as `logs:Get*`.
  - A permission set has no native single JSON file; say which API shapes the file follows.
  - Raw log reads (`logs:GetLogEvents`) and `lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration` are allowed per service only (`framework.md:126-131`).
  - The test proves only that the listed actions are absent; say that.
- **E1:** the pinned required-check source app is gap G19. Mark `integration_id` as a placeholder that depends on G19.
- **E9:** `plugin validate` checks the manifest schema, not that every source is pinned to a `sha`. Add a test for that; it can also raise R1.4.1b from "link only" to ✅.
- **E10:** say explicitly that `tsc` proves only that the code compiles, not that the policies trigger.
- **§1 #7:** `docs/problem-control-map.md` still says "Status: draft for owner review" (line 3). The plan keeps it "như hiện tại" without getting owner approval or updating the status.
- **Step 6 sync:** the sync must also update `docs/adr/README.md` lines 3-4 and its "rollout plan (layer 8)" line after the split, and `framework.md:20` ("Nothing here was checked locally (✅)") once examples carry ✅ output.

**Rule compliance:** Clean. There are no secrets or PII, the placeholders are correct, the note has a Vietnamese body with an English summary, and no step touches live infrastructure.

**Verdict:** Not ready. There is 1 HIGH (the E4 `sub` format contradicts the immutable-format assumption, R3.7 A2) and 9 MEDIUM, mostly overstated validation and gaps against framing Q14 and the framework; all can be fixed in the note without new design decisions.
